summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with mast cell activation syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, and organizing pneumonia was admitted for pneumonia with symptoms of productive cough, fever, and dyspnea. She also reported epigastric pain, nausea, and itching consistent with her usual mast cell flares. A chest CT confirmed improvement in known organizing pneumonia lesions but revealed a new small lung nodule to be followed in six months and incidental low-density splenic lesions requiring outpatient ultrasound. She was treated with azithromycin and cefpodoxime for pneumonia. After multidisciplinary review, IV narcotics and antihistamines were discontinued, and she was managed with oral medications. The team concluded her symptoms did not represent anaphylaxis, and she was advised to develop a formal pain management plan with her pain specialist. She remained stable, required no pain medications by discharge, and was sent home with instructions to complete antibiotics and follow up with her providers.
